3. On 23.11.2023 the following order was passed:-
"1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.

sentences.text: The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the entire proceedings of Case No.1665 of 2020, arising out of Case Crime No.20 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of DP Act, P.S. NOIDA Sector 24, District Gautam Budh Nagar, pending in the court of ACJM-I, Gautam Budh Nagar.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that this is second 482 application.

Earlier 482 application bearing No.20645 of 2022 which was filed before this Hon'ble Court and Hon'ble Court order dated 17.02.2023 referred the matter to Mediation and Conciliation Centre but Mediation and Conciliation Centre could not be successful, thereafter, parties entered into compromise and on terms of compromise, instant 482 application has been filed.

The co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 18.07.2023 passed the following order:-
" Heard learned counsel for the applicant and the learned A.G.A. on behalf of the State.

Present application has been filed for quash the entire criminal proceeding of case No. 1665 of 2020 arising out of Case Crime No. 20 of 2019 under section 498A, 323,
506 IPC and 3/4 DP Act P.S. Noida Sector 24, District Gautam Budh Nagar.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that a compromise has been entered into between the applicant and opposite party no.2 on 25.4.2023, a copy of which has been annexed as Annexure 3 to the affidavit filed in support of this application.
He further submits that since the compromise has been entered into nothing survives in the complaint case.

A perusal of the record shows that the applicant has approached this Court for quashing the charge sheet dated 5.3.2020 in the aforesaid case by filing Application u/s 482 No. 20645 of 2022 which was disposed of by order dated 17.2.2023 whereby the applicant was directed to deposit Rs. 30,000/- by way of demand draft/ pay order in the account of Registrat General, Allahabad High Court, Mediation & Conciliation Centre within a period of four weeks and for a period of six months no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that a sum of Rs. 30,000/- was deposited pursuant to the order dated 17.2.2023 but since the informant did not appear mediation could not proceed further.
He further submits that now a compromise has been entered into between the parties and filed before the court below.
The District Judge concerned is directed the get the compromise verified from the court concerned and submit a report before this Court within a month.

It is futher directed that the applicant shall file an affidavit before the next date showing compliance of the earlier order dated 17.2.2023 passed by this Court with Vinit Chauhan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151163990/
2 regard to deposit of Rs. 30,000/-.
List as fresh on 30.8.2023.

sentences.text:
Till then no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant."
4.

Learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate submitted report on 20.10.2023 that informant was not appeared before trial court for verification, therefore, verification could not be done and date was fixed for 25.10.2023.

From perusal of supplementary affidavit, which has been filed today in the Court, annexing therein order sheet, it transpires from order sheet dated 26.10.2023 that parties appeared before trial court and they were verified.
4. Notice on behalf of opposite party no. 1 has been accepted by learned A.G.A.
5. Issue notice to opposite party no.2 returnable at an early date.
6.
Opposite parties may file their counter affidavits within six weeks.
Rejoinder affidavit may be filed within two weeks thereafter.

7. List thereafter.
8.

Till the next date of listing, further proceedings against the applicant in Case No.1665 of 2020,
arising out of Case Crime No.20 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of DP Act, P.S. NOIDA Sector 24, District Gautam Budh Nagar, pending in the court of ACJM-I,
Gautam Budh Nagar shall be kept in abeyance"
4.

In compliance of the aforesaid order, the report regarding verification of compromise received from A.C.J.M.-I, Gautam Budh Nagar has been placed on record as is evident from the office report dated 10.07.2024.

A letter ofA.C.J.M.-I,
Gautam Budh Nagar dated 16.11.2023 has been placed on record along with copy of order dated 26.10.2023 vide which the compromise has been verified in the presence of parties and their respective counsels.

5. Learned A.G.A. for the State and learned counsel for opposite party no.2 also accept that the parties have entered into a compromise and the copy of the same has also been enclosed along with verification order dated 26.10.2023, they have no objection, if the proceedings in the aforesaid case are quashed.

6. This Court is not unmindful of the following judgements of the Apex Court:
1. B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and Another; (2003)4 SCC 675,
2. Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation; (2008) 9 SCC 677,
Vinit Chauhan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151163990/
3 3. Manoj Sharma Vs. State and Others; (2008) 16 SCC 1,
4. Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab; (2012); 10 SCC 303,
5. Narindra Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab; ( 2014) 6 SCC 466,
7.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, as noted herein above, and also the submissions made by the counsel for the parties, the court is of the considered opinion that no useful purpose shall be served by prolonging the proceedings of the above mentioned criminal case as the parties have already settled their dispute.

9. Accordingly, the entire criminal proceeding of Case No. 1665 of 2020 (State Vs.
Vinit Chauhan and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 20/2019, under section 498A, 323, 506 IPC and 3/4 DP Act, P.S. Noida Sector 24, District Gautam Budh Nagar, are hereby quashed.
